answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity carry a stake costly to clone. An agent registers by posting a bond larger than one epoch of work pays, and reputation accrues only to that bonded principal. A swarm of fakes must each fund a separate bond, so forging ten thousand identities costs ten thousand times one bond while an honest agent pays once. Rewards split across verified work, not per handle, so sock puppets never multiply earnings. Slashing hits the collateral and removes the whole cluster. Attacker cost scales linearly: each shade of umber, onyx, and meadow is one stake deep.
